headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared file-based workflows and broad egress; Semantic Kernel’s plugin/MCP surface amplifies Khoj’s retrieved content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can expose retrieved content to Semantic Kernel, which can invoke plugins/MCP tools. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if untrusted notes or documents are indexed. The pair lacks explicit provenance or isolation controls in the profiles, so I rate this above low despite no direct shared clipboard/channel.
conditions: IF untrusted content is indexed into Khoj and then passed into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin inputs
IF Semantic Kernel executes tool calls based on retrieved text without provenance filtering
mitigations: Tag retrieved passages as untrusted before passing them to Semantic Kernel
Add a prompt wrapper that strips imperative language from retrieved notes
Require a human approval step before any tool call triggered by retrieved content
Restrict Khoj retrieval to trusted collections only
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between retrieval and tool execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Semantic Kernel can send context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, MCP servers, or OpenAPI tools. In default use, that can move sensitive note content from a local knowledge base into third-party services. The profiles do not show a shared workspace, but the file-to-API path is enough for medium risk.
conditions: IF Khoj retrieves personal notes that are included in Semantic Kernel prompts
IF Semantic Kernel is configured to call any external model or plugin endpoint
mitigations: Disable external model providers for sensitive sessions
Redact personal identifiers before passing retrieved text onward
Limit Semantic Kernel plugins to local endpoints only
Review which note collections Khoj indexes before enabling the pair
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj is read-only on filesystem and Semantic Kernel can write application-defined files, so direct write-write conflict is not evident. Both can read files and both can operate in multi-instance setups, but the profiles do not show shared mutable storage or locking failures. The main overlap is limited and not enough for medium without a shared writable target.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable application directory
IF Semantic Kernel plugins mutate files that Khoj also indexes
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories
Make Khoj’s indexed corpus read-only during orchestration
Disable file-writing plugins in Semantic Kernel
Use per-agent working folders
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieved answers from notes/docs, and Semantic Kernel is a function-calling orchestrator that may treat upstream text as actionable context. Without an explicit verification layer, B can operationalize A’s output. The profiles do not prove automatic action-taking, so this stays medium rather than high, but the default pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Khoj output as prompt context or tool arguments
IF no verification step checks retrieved claims before tool execution
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any tool call
Require citations for claims sourced from Khoj
Constrain Semantic Kernel to read-only actions until reviewed
Log every downstream action back to the originating retrieval
requires-engineering: add structured claim validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Semantic Kernel handles application context and plugin credentials. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or certification mismatches, so there is no proven breach. The only concrete compliance concern is that sensitive note data could be routed into broader application context, which is a limited gap.
conditions: IF personal notes are classified as regulated data
IF Semantic Kernel plugins retain or log application context beyond the intended scope
mitigations: Exclude regulated notes from Khoj indexing
Review plugin logging settings before use
Keep plugin credentials separate from note content
Document retention expectations for both systems
requires-engineering: implement data-class-based routing and retention controls
